hook: Last video's quiz answer: one thousand two hundred and fifty rupees. Well done if you got it!
Now, C B S E Class Eleven. T. S. Graywaal, Question thirty-five.
Purchases are already adjusted, and one adjustment is hidden in the trial balance.
Can you spot it? Let's solve it together.
question: Here is the question. The trial balance of Shubho, on thirty-first March, twenty twenty-six.

Debit side: land and building, purchases adjusted, stock, wages, salaries, office expenses, carriage, discount, bad debts, insurance, plant and machinery, furniture, drawings, debtors, bank, and office equipments.
Credit side: discount received, sales, capital, Chatterjee's loan, commission, creditors, and expenses payable.
Both sides total five lakh sixty-six thousand eight hundred and fifty rupees.
Now look carefully. Purchases are adjusted. And Chatterjee's loan was taken on first October, at eighteen percent.
adjust: One. Depreciate land and building at six percent, plant and machinery at ten, office equipments at twenty, and furniture and fixtures at fifteen percent.
Two. Create provision for doubtful debts at two percent on sundry debtors.
Three. Insurance includes two hundred and fifty rupees paid in advance.
Four. Provide salary to Shubho, fifteen thousand rupees per annum.
Five. Outstanding salaries, eleven thousand five hundred.
Six. Ten percent of the net profit is to be transferred to general reserve.
Pause the video, and try it yourself. Then check with me.
hidden: First, read the trial balance carefully. Three items need attention.
Purchases are adjusted, and stock is as on thirty-first March. So this stock is the closing stock.
Closing stock is already deducted from purchases. So it does not go to the trading account. Show forty-five thousand only in the balance sheet.
Expenses payable, three thousand three hundred, is already a liability in the trial balance. Just show it in the balance sheet.
And the hidden one. Chatterjee's loan of twenty-five thousand was taken on first October, at eighteen percent per annum. No interest is in the trial balance.
Twenty-five thousand into eighteen over hundred, into six over twelve. Two thousand two hundred and fifty rupees outstanding.
Debit interest to profit and loss, and add it to the loan in the balance sheet.
a1: Adjustment four. Salary to Shubho, the proprietor.
This salary of fifteen thousand is only provided, not paid. So it is not drawings.
It is treated like interest on capital. Debit profit and loss account with fifteen thousand.
And credit Shubho's capital account. Add fifteen thousand to capital in the balance sheet.
a2: Adjustments three and five. Outstanding salaries and prepaid insurance.
Salaries, thirty-nine thousand, plus outstanding eleven thousand five hundred. Fifty thousand five hundred.
Add salary to Shubho, fifteen thousand. Salaries in profit and loss, sixty-five thousand five hundred.
Insurance, fifteen hundred, less prepaid two hundred and fifty. Twelve hundred and fifty.
Outstanding salaries is a liability, and prepaid insurance is an asset.
a3: Adjustment two. Provision for doubtful debts.
Debtors, forty thousand into two over hundred. Provision, eight hundred rupees.
There is no old provision. So charge to profit and loss: bad debts twelve hundred, plus provision eight hundred. Two thousand.
In the balance sheet, debtors forty thousand, less eight hundred. Thirty-nine thousand two hundred.
a4: Land and building, fifty thousand into six over hundred. Three thousand.
Plant and machinery, fifty thousand into ten over hundred. Five thousand.
Office equipments, twelve thousand into twenty over hundred. Two thousand four hundred.
Furniture and fixtures, twenty thousand into fifteen over hundred. Three thousand.
Total depreciation, thirteen thousand four hundred rupees, goes to profit and loss.
trading: Now the trading account of Shubho, for the year ended thirty-first March, twenty twenty-six.
To purchases, adjusted, two lakh seven thousand five hundred. No opening stock, because purchases are adjusted.
To wages, forty-five thousand three hundred. To carriage inwards, twelve hundred.
Credit side. By sales, three lakh eighty-three thousand five hundred. No closing stock here.
Total, three lakh eighty-three thousand five hundred. Gross profit, one lakh twenty-nine thousand five hundred rupees.
pl: Next, the profit and loss account.
Credit side. Gross profit, one lakh twenty-nine thousand five hundred. Discount received, twelve hundred. Commission, fifteen hundred. Total, one lakh thirty-two thousand two hundred.
Debit side. Salaries, thirty-nine thousand, plus outstanding eleven thousand five hundred, plus salary to Shubho fifteen thousand. Sixty-five thousand five hundred.
Office expenses, fifteen thousand four hundred. Carriage outwards, two thousand. Discount allowed, seven hundred and fifty.
Bad debts and provision, two thousand. Insurance, twelve hundred and fifty. Interest on Chatterjee's loan, two thousand two hundred and fifty.
Profit before transfer, twenty-nine thousand six hundred and fifty. Ten percent to general reserve, two thousand nine hundred and sixty-five.
Net profit, twenty-six thousand six hundred and eighty-five rupees.
bs: Finally, the balance sheet of Shubho, as at thirty-first March, twenty twenty-six.
Capital, one lakh fifteen thousand. Add salary to Shubho, fifteen thousand. Add net profit, twenty-six thousand six hundred and eighty-five.
Less drawings, twenty thousand. Capital, one lakh thirty-six thousand six hundred and eighty-five.
General reserve, two thousand nine hundred and sixty-five. Chatterjee's loan, twenty-five thousand, plus interest outstanding, two thousand two hundred and fifty.

Creditors, thirty-seven thousand three hundred and fifty. Expenses payable, three thousand three hundred. Outstanding salaries, eleven thousand five hundred. Total, two lakh nineteen thousand and fifty.
Assets. Land and building, forty-seven thousand. Plant and machinery, forty-five thousand. Furniture, seventeen thousand. Office equipments, nine thousand six hundred.
Closing stock, forty-five thousand. Debtors, thirty-nine thousand two hundred. Prepaid insurance, two hundred and fifty. Bank, sixteen thousand.
Assets total, two lakh nineteen thousand and fifty. The balance sheet tallies!
traps: Four exam traps from this question.
Trap one. Purchases are adjusted. So the closing stock goes only to the balance sheet, not to the trading account.
Trap two. The hidden interest. Loan at eighteen percent from first October. Six months interest, two thousand two hundred and fifty.
Trap three. Salary to the proprietor is not drawings. Debit profit and loss, and add it to capital.
Trap four. General reserve is ten percent of the profit before transfer. Twenty-nine thousand six hundred and fifty gives two thousand nine hundred and sixty-five.
recap: Gross profit, one lakh twenty-nine thousand five hundred.
Net profit, twenty-six thousand six hundred and eighty-five.
Balance sheet total, two lakh nineteen thousand and fifty, on both sides.
Remember: when purchases are adjusted, closing stock goes only to the balance sheet.
